methodology: Loaded every executable mock module from src/data/mocks/icfes-mock-01.ts through icfes-mock-23.ts and confirmed the runtime shape and exact count for every section and question.
Read every stimulus, passage, stem, option set and current key; evaluated grammar, naturalness, clarity, key defensibility, distractor plausibility and stimulus-question-option coherence.

Inspected the executable guided adapter in src/data/icfes/guided-mocks.ts because the source mocks contain no explicit per-item explanations and the product generates all 1,035 explanations at runtime.

Ran deterministic checks for duplicate options, answer bounds, exact prompt/stimulus duplication and answer-position distributions. Automated checks were treated as inventory evidence only, never as semantic approval.
Recorded uncertain cases as needs-adjudication and did not edit questions, keys, code, catalogues or release state.

checks.evidence: 23/23 mocks and 1,035/1,035 questions reviewed; 45 questions and seven sections in every mock.
All keys are in range and no item contains duplicate normalized options.
Multiple visible grammar, naturalness, factual-coherence and key-defensibility defects remain; mock-20:p5q3 has no option that answers its stem.
The runtime adapter misclassifies all Part 1, Part 2 and Part 7 items, producing structurally false explanation/rationale templates for 460 questions.
B/C contain 145/161 Part 5 keys, 100/115 Part 6 keys and 213/230 Part 7 keys, creating a learnable answer-position cue.
This actor is a reviewer, not the human adjudicator or release warden.

findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Map the actual notice task to functional_texts/notice and generate notice-based evidence and rationales for all 115 affected questions.
findings.evidence: Every source mock labels Part 1 as notices/instructions, but guided-mocks.ts:9-16 maps Part 1 to vocabulary_basic/word-match; lines 235-244 then produce definition-based explanations and lines 352-377 attach the wrong skill, label, strategy and micro-lesson.

findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Map the actual vocabulary-matching task to vocabulary_basic/word-match and use the question definition plus vocabulary glosses for all 115 affected questions.
findings.evidence: Every source mock labels Part 2 as vocabulary matching, but guided-mocks.ts maps Part 2 to functional_texts/notice and uses only the section topic as evidence, yielding claims such as an alleged notice named 'Health' that supposedly supports 'cough'.

findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Treat these 230 items as extended reading questions; generate localized evidence and question-specific rationales rather than cloze substitutions.
findings.evidence: All source Part 7 sections are reading passages with ten comprehension questions. guided-mocks.ts:9-16 classifies Part 7 as lexical-cloze; lines 211-244 pass the whole passage to a substitution template even though the stems contain no blank, and lines 331-340 repeat that false method for every distractor.

findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Do not emit editorialStatus='reviewed' or reviewedAt for generated items until an independent hash-bound review and adjudication have actually passed.
findings.evidence: guided-mocks.ts:381-383 assigns reviewedAt='2026-08-03' and editorialStatus='reviewed' automatically to every adapted item. The prior audit relied on structural checks and contains zero semantic findings, while this independent review finds production blockers.

findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rebalance answer positions per mock and part by moving complete option texts, then re-review every touched item's semantic key and regenerate hashes.
findings.evidence: 90.1% of Part 5, 87.0% of Part 6 and 92.6% of Part 7 keys occur in positions B or C. The repeated position cue is strong enough to reward guessing behavior and weakens distractor validity.

findings.currentKey: C: It has increased legal protections for indigenous people in the forest.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Replace 'Brazil, the largest Amazon country' with a precise formulation such as 'Brazil, which contains the largest share of the Amazon rainforest'.
findings.evidence: The phrase 'the largest Amazon country' is nonstandard and semantically ambiguous: it can wrongly imply that Brazil is an entity called an 'Amazon country' ranked by overall area rather than by its share of the rainforest.

findings.currentKey: C: The high cost of living makes raising children more difficult.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Change 'to have fewer than previous generations' to 'to have fewer children than couples did in previous generations'.
findings.evidence: The current comparison grammatically compares the omitted noun 'children' with 'previous generations', not the number of children chosen by couples across time.

findings.currentKey: C: determination
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Keep the semantic key only if the passage is corrected to 'the passion and determination of Colombian athletes often compensate for these differences'.
findings.evidence: The compound subject 'passion and determination' requires plural 'compensate'; the source currently says 'often compensates'. The learner sees an untested grammar error inside a grammar-cloze passage.

findings.currentKey: C: Better regulation and safety training is a better solution than banning extreme sports.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Better regulation and safety training are a better solution than banning extreme sports.
findings.evidence: The keyed option has a compound subject joined by 'and' but uses singular 'is'. A correct-answer option in an English assessment cannot itself contain this agreement error.

findings.currentKey: C: history
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: needs-adjudication: consider adding 'heritage' as the intended key and rebuilding distractors, or rewrite the sentence so 'history' is the unambiguously natural noun.
findings.evidence: 'Colombia has a rich and varied musical history' is grammatical, but the remainder describes living regional forms, instruments and intergenerational continuity, for which 'musical heritage' is more precise. The intended construct is unclear.

findings.currentKey: C: popularity
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: needs-adjudication: use 'cultural significance/importance' if the UNESCO designation is the evidence, or add evidence that genuinely supports global popularity.
findings.evidence: Recognition as intangible cultural heritage establishes cultural significance, not necessarily 'global popularity'. The keyed noun is grammatically possible but the causal claim is not semantically well supported.

findings.currentKey: C: Because its temperatures are mild and pleasant throughout the year.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite as 'Medellín, located at around 1,500 metres above sea level, is often described as the city of eternal spring...'.
findings.evidence: The source says 'the weather is often described as the city of eternal spring', equating weather with a city. This category error is visible in the sentence that directly supports the keyed answer.

findings.currentKey: B: Yes, it is considered some of the best quality.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Yes, it is considered to be of some of the highest quality. Alternatively: Yes, it is considered among the best in the world.
findings.evidence: 'Considered some of the best quality' is not a natural complement pattern; the keyed conversational response needs 'to be of' or 'among'.

findings.currentKey: C: Whether investing more in tourism is the right priority for Colombia
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Correct 'Supporers of tourism investment' to 'Supporters of tourism investment'.
findings.evidence: The first word of the pro-investment paragraph is misspelled 'Supporers', a visible error in a passage used for ten scored questions.

findings.currentKey: D: They achieved impressive results
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: needs-adjudication: replace this tautological item with a claim supported by a specific result, or add a concrete outcome to the passage before asking about it.
findings.evidence: The stem asks what schools achieved and the keyed option merely repeats the passage's content-free phrase 'with impressive results'. It measures phrase matching rather than comprehension and provides no specific proposition to defend.

findings.currentKey: A: It is a condition of graduation
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite option A as 'Complete community service hours' and make every distractor an action, or change the stem to ask why students participate and rebuild all options. Re-adjudicate the item after either change.
findings.evidence: Stem: 'What do some universities require students to do before graduating?' None of the four options is a verb phrase answering what students must do. The keyed sentence answers why the activity matters, not what is required.

findings.currentKey: B: hitting the ball fewer times.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite the supporting sentence as 'In both formats, the golfer with the lowest total number of strokes across all holes wins.'
findings.evidence: The passage says 'the golf player with the lowest number of strokes for all the holes, wins': 'golf player' is less natural than 'golfer', 'for all the holes' is awkward and the comma incorrectly separates subject and verb.

findings.currentKey: B: A sense of respect towards variety.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite the passage and key using natural educational English: 'respect for diversity', 'express themselves as individuals', 'teamwork', and 'prisoners of war'. Re-adjudicate all five questions against the revised passage.
findings.evidence: The passage contains repeated non-native phrasing ('exploring arts', 'individual humans', 'cultural variety', 'promoting work in teams', 'war prisoners'), while the keyed option 'respect towards variety' is itself unnatural and less precise than 'respect for diversity'.

findings.currentKey: B: It turned into a relaxing moment of reflection.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite the full passage before reuse; minimally use 'wait in a queue/line', 'made me think about what life is all about', and a coherent formulation of the remembered/productive moments. Re-adjudicate p7q1-p7q10.
findings.evidence: The passage includes 'wait in a row', 'made me think what life is all about', 'remember until the deepest nostalgia' and 'greatest moments of active and efficient time'. The latter two are semantically incoherent, so generated explanations cannot reliably teach from this stimulus.

findings.currentKey: A: seen how patients value nurses.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite the full nurse passage in natural, non-exaggerated English before retaining its keys; replace claims about 'nice with people', finding an ambulance, going to a drugstore for days, an 'awesome time' in hospital and nurses working through all free time.
findings.evidence: Multiple sentences are grammatically awkward or logically implausible: 'really nice with people', 'they found an ambulance', 'I only had to go to the drugstore for a few days', 'This awesome time at the hospital', 'thankful for their excellent job', and the blanket claim that nurses spend even their free time learning.

findings.currentKey: B: Looking forward to having some spare time? Take a career break and learn about its advantages.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: needs-adjudication: replace the announcement options with grammatical summaries that cover the text's three claims; the key should mention a gap year rather than reduce it to spare time or a career break.
findings.evidence: The keyed announcement is a weak and partly misleading summary for a passage about language immersion, reflection and CV-building; 'looking forward to spare time' is not the stated motivation, and a gap year is not always a career break.

findings.currentKey: A: were born after the 80s.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Replace the false definition with a verified birth-year range and rewrite the passage in natural English; then re-adjudicate p7q1-p7q10.
findings.evidence: The passage inaccurately defines millennials as all people born after the 1980s and contains sustained non-native phrasing ('mistake about my age', 'that person is accurate', 'cosmetic operations', 'let their skin feel the sun', 'arbitrary age opinion', 'not fair to their identities'). The keyed option perpetuates the false definition.

findings.currentKey: C: go to the post office.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite the passage for idiomatic English while preserving the intended claims; examples include 'writing letters is not as quick or easy', 'letters take time to write', 'written in a loved one's hand', and 'writing a letter creates something tangible'.
findings.evidence: The current passage repeatedly uses awkward structures ('Using letters is not as easy and fast', 'take them to the post office', 'writing as an act that repairs', 'written by the hand', 'do many things with various windows open', 'Writing a letter is building').

findings.currentKey: D: Describing how the babysitting experience has been extraordinary for her.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite the interview using 'majored in Child and Youth Studies', 'most satisfying aspect', and a natural account of how her passion developed; then re-adjudicate all five questions and all distractors.
findings.evidence: The passage says 'using babysitting to pay for her college, where she decided to take Child & Youth Studies as a degree', asks for the 'most satisfactory aspect', and says 'become my passion as much as it has'. Several distractors also contain malformed phrasing such as 'work day hours only'.

findings.currentKey: B: Advising her daughter on how to enjoy camp and life.
findings.proposedKeyOrWording: Rewrite the passage using 'experiences she would have', a consistent future time reference, and 'I hope you feel excited'; then re-adjudicate all ten questions.
findings.evidence: The source uses 'events she would get to live', combines 'has been' with 'the first time she'd go', and says 'I wish you get excited'. These are salient grammatical/naturalness defects in the central framing and quoted advice.

handoff.reason: The bank cannot receive an English-specialist PASS while a scored item has no valid response, 460 paid guided explanations use the wrong task model, and multiple passages/keyed options contain material errors.
